interactions.summary: Jiang responds to the online paradox about a God who contains everything, develops a model of God as eternity plus becoming through humans, fields a student question about why God created hate, listens to an absence-of-love analogy, and says the issue will be answered later when the class reaches the angels.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Moderator relay, Jiang exposition, student question, student comparison, Jiang reply

interactions.summary: A student reads the verse in which the apostolic light delights in Dante's answer and circles him three times, marking the successful completion of the faith exam.

Jiang says Dante has passed the first test on faith and is moving to a second exam on hope, then a student reads the opening of Canto 25 where Dante imagines returning to Florence for the laurel crown.

claims.claim: Jiang defines God here as eternal and infinite, the source that encompasses everything rather than one being among others.
He argues that God is both being and becoming, and that the paradox is resolved by treating humans as part of God through whom becoming occurs.
Jiang says humans represent infinity while God represents eternity, allowing human becoming to take place inside the divine whole.
He postpones the full answer to why hate exists by saying the class will later see that angels are incapable of hatred and that hate is somehow necessary.
Jiang marks the end of the faith examination and says the next apostolic test in Paradise will be about hope under James.

signature_moments.moment: The paradox of God containing both stable being and changing becoming is solved by placing human becoming inside God itself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: humans are part of the of god itself
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's most compact metaphysical move in the packet and turns the class's abstract paradox into a human-divine structure.

signature_moments.moment: Hate is not simply denied; Jiang promises that later heaven itself will show why hate is somehow necessary.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you will understand why hate is necessary
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves a sharp, potentially surprising claim that could matter later in the episode read or semantic bundle.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's formula for a God who is stable source and also the encompassing condition within which human change occurs.
The second theological virtue Dante is about to be examined on after successfully answering the first test on faith.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang promises a later explanation for why hate is necessary but does not yet supply the mechanism in this packet, so the claim should be carried forward as unresolved lecture pressure.
